title: Your Agent, On Your Phone
subtitle: Wednesday your Session 4 agent becomes a personal Telegram bot your friends can text. The Wednesday after, you close the three holes a business would never accept: a door, an approval gate inside the chat, and a memory that survives — and can be erased.
heroTitle: Your Agent, On Your Phone

objectives.title: Take the Agent Out of Colab
objectives.description: Wrap the loop you wrote in Session 4 in a Telegram bot. Your phone is the interface, Colab is the server for now, and a downloaded bot.py runs it on your laptop with no Colab at all.

objectives.title: Give It Real Tools
objectives.description: A live job board with no key, Adzuna local listings with an optional key that fall back honestly, and a weather API that fails the interesting way: not with an error, with a confident wrong answer.

objectives.title: Close the Three Holes
objectives.description: Anyone can use it, it acts without asking, it forgets when the cell stops. An allow-list, an approval gate that asks you on your phone, and memory on disk with a /forget command.

objectives.title: Ask the Four Questions
objectives.description: Who can use it? What can it do without asking? What does it remember, and can it forget? What happens when the API is wrong? The questions to put to any AI product a vendor shows you.

activities.title: Put It On Your Phone (Wed Oct 7)
activities.description: Parts 1–6 of the Meeting 1 notebook, on your own keys:

steps.title: Make a bot
steps.description: BotFather → /newbot → copy the token into Colab Secrets. Your Gemini key from Session 3 is already there.

steps.title: Paste your HW #5 tool
steps.description: Part 2 has a marked slot. Register the declaration and the function. Now the bot is yours.

steps.title: Run the bridge
steps.description: Part 4 is the bot. While the cell runs, open your bot on your phone and say hi.

steps.title: Break it, then swap
steps.description: Math, jobs, 'which pays most', the Boston query. Then a neighbor's bot with your question — two phones, two memories.

steps.title: Download bot.py
steps.description: Part 6 writes one standalone file. python bot.py on your laptop, no Colab.

activities.title: Close the Three Holes (Wed Oct 14)

steps.title: The door
steps.description: Text /whoami, put your id in ALLOWED, re-run. Your neighbor now gets '🔒 private assistant' and their own id.

steps.title: The gate
steps.description: Ask it to email someone. 🚦 Reply no, then ask if it sent. Ask again, reply yes. Two audit rows: BLOCKED, SENT.

steps.title: Memory that survives
steps.description: Stop the cell. Run it again. Ask what you emailed earlier. Then /forget — in memory and on disk.

steps.title: The API that guesses
steps.description: Weather in Boston, then in 'Bostn'. Does the agent notice it got Sweden? Then 'Xyzzyville' — an honest error.

activities.discussionNote: The loop is still 40 lines. Everything you added this week is the part a company actually pays for.

takeaways.text: The interface is not the agent. Phone, Slack, web form, Telegram — the loop can't tell the difference. The interface is the cheap part.
Abstract the provider, and make the tool confess. Adzuna or the fallback board, the workflow never changed. The FALLBACK label is what stops the model from lying for you.
A door, a gate, a memory you can erase. Allow-list, approval inside the chat, memory on disk with /forget. The three things that turn a demo into something a company can run.
Real APIs don't fail. They guess. Return what the service actually matched, and tell the model to say so. Your agent's reputation is decided in that 1%.
Ask the four questions. Who can use it, what can it do without asking, what does it remember and can it forget, what happens when the API is wrong.
